answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on reputation decay for idle identities, capped per identity per epoch, no identity may audit its own recruit. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The opal of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Work waits on the kernel until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the river of the next round.
